title: Streamline Workspace Hopper: adaptive micro-navigation and session-aware routing
creator: Sana Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, session-aware workspace hopper that reduces cognitive load when switching contexts in the Redwood Console. The component should adapt to user activity (recent routes, pinned dashboards, ongoing rollouts) and provide lightweight routing with permission-aware actions. Goal is to reduce average workspace switch time and accidental navigation into high-cost routes.
background: Current sidebar + command-palette patterns surface a large sea of destinations; users commonly lose track of which workspace contains active rollouts or cost-sensitive dashboards. Engineering telemetry shows a 14% accidental navigation rate to high-cost endpoints during demo flows. This initiative aims to replace one-off quick-switch UIs with a predictable, micro-nav component that is discoverable and consistent across hosted and dedicated tenant types.
design_goals: Make workspace switching <2 clicks for most frequent flows
Surface active rollouts and cost hotspots inline in the switcher
Respect RBAC: only show actions permitted by the user
Provide graceful fallbacks for long lists (fuzzy search + recency + pinned)
Be resilient to high-latency catalog calls (optimistic local cache + lightweight skeletons)
constraints_and_tradeoffs: Won't replace the full left rail in this phase to limit scope; this is a complementary micro-nav
Prefetching recent-workspaces improves UX but increases client memory and potential stale state
Inline cost badges require a sampled-cost API rather than full compute to avoid slowing the component
Scoped to desktop and large tablet; mobile layout deferred to a follow-up
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype reviewed and signed-off by PM and Eng (link above)
Prototype demonstrates session-awareness: recent, pinned, and active-rollout buckets
Design tokens and accessibility heuristics documented (keyboard navigation, screen reader labels)
Hand-off package containing component states, microcopy, and animations delivered to frontend team
A/B test plan drafted for rollout measuring: switch time, accidental navigation rate, and engagement with cost badges
review_feedback: PM asks to include a lightweight confirmation when navigating into Dedicated-only clusters
Eng suggests optimistic UI first-run cache with background reconciliation to hide network jitter
Accessibility reviewer requests ARIA live region announcements for active-rollout changes
Cost team recommends capped precision for inline badges and link to expanded cost view
decisions: Use a three-tier ordering: Recents > Pinned > Active Rollouts; fuzzy search appended below
Inline cost badges will show 'approx' values with tooltip linking to full cost dashboard
Micro-nav will be mountable from left-rail, topbar, and command palette to maximize discoverability
Defer mobile reflow and multi-tenant impersonation support to follow-up cycle
engineering_notes: Frontend: React + Redwood design-system component. Use local IndexedDB for short-term recency cache and Background Sync for reconciliation. Backend: add sampled-cost endpoint (cost/preview) and compact rollouts list (rollouts/active-summary). Performance budget: initial render <= 120ms on cold start for typical catalog of 120 workspaces.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cost badges could mislead users if sampling diverges. Mitigation: add clear "approx" affordance and link to full-cost view
Risk: RBAC complexity may cause flicker when permissions load. Mitigation: show skeleton entries with disabled actions until permission check completes
Risk: Increased client storage for recency cache. Mitigation: bound entries to 200 and purge LRU
next_steps: Resolve engineering PR comments and merge - assigned to ENG-frontend team
Run a moderated usability test with 6 customers on 2026-03-20
Prepare A/B experiment in Growth with tracking plan and success metrics
Schedule design handoff meeting and record component token matrix
